items.usage: 指同時帶來好處與壞處的事物，常搭配 become / prove to be / is a double-edged sword。
items.example: Social media is a double-edged sword for small businesses: it offers free exposure but also invites public criticism.
items.trans: 社群媒體對小型企業來說是把雙面刃：它提供免費曝光，但也招來公開批評。

items.term: a whole host of + 複數名詞
items.usage: 比 a lot of 正式，強調「種類多」，常用於列舉前。
items.example: The new software update fixes a whole host of security issues.
items.trans: 這次軟體更新修補了一大堆安全漏洞。

items.usage: 文中指「從源頭（預防問題發生）」。另一常見用法是質疑語氣：Why did you agree in the first place?（你當初幹嘛答應？）
items.example: The best way to deal with debt is not to get into it in the first place.
items.trans: 處理債務最好的方法，就是一開始別欠債。

items.usage: 口語偏多，帶點「完全搞不清楚狀況」的意味。文中加上 fairly 緩和語氣。與 #84 have no clue 同一家族。
items.example: When I started my first job, I was completely clueless about how expense reports worked.
items.trans: 我剛開始第一份工作時，完全不知道報帳是怎麼運作的。

items.term: be under immense pressure to + V
items.usage: immense 可替換為 enormous / intense / mounting。
items.example: The sales team is under immense pressure to hit their quarterly targets.
items.trans: 業務團隊承受著極大壓力，必須達成季度目標。

items.usage: 受詞常為 a plan / a task / research / a procedure / an experiment，比 do 正式。
items.example: The audit was carried out by an independent firm.
items.trans: 這次稽核是由一家獨立的公司執行的。

items.usage: = precisely，但放在句尾更有力。常見 with great precision。
items.example: The robot arm can assemble tiny components with remarkable precision.
items.trans: 這支機械手臂能以驚人的精準度組裝微小零件。

items.usage: 強調「勉力應對」困境或壓力，比 deal with 多了「辛苦」的感覺。
items.example: Many employees struggled to cope with the sudden shift to remote work.
items.trans: 許多員工難以應付突然轉為遠端工作的變化。

items.usage: 指一口一口地抽，畫面感強。
items.example: He sat on the porch, puffing on his pipe and watching the sunset.
items.trans: 他坐在門廊上，抽著菸斗看夕陽。

items.usage: 醫療、安全相關文章的高頻搭配，也常見 potentially dangerous / costly / harmful。近義見 #113 lethal。
items.example: Mixing these two medications can cause a potentially fatal reaction.
items.trans: 混用這兩種藥物可能會引起致命的反應。

items.usage: 常形容資訊、人口、植被。sparse information、sparsely populated（人口稀少的）。
items.example: Details about the merger remain sparse.
items.trans: 關於這次合併的細節仍然很少。

items.usage: 可及物也可不及物。accumulate wealth / knowledge / experience；Dust accumulated on the shelves.
items.example: Over the years, she has accumulated a wealth of experience in project management.
items.trans: 這些年來，她在專案管理上累積了豐富的經驗。

items.usage: 形容詞為 inept（#156）。作者用它指「有知識卻無法正確運用」，不是單純的無知（ignorance）。
items.example: The company's losses were blamed on the ineptitude of its management.
items.trans: 公司的虧損被歸咎於管理層的無能。

items.usage: 比 at the same time 正式，寫作常用。
items.example: The film will be released simultaneously in theaters and online.
items.trans: 這部電影將在戲院和線上同步上映。

items.meaning: 壓倒性的、令人難以招架的
items.usage: 兩種意思：①令人喘不過氣（an overwhelming workload）；②壓倒性的（an overwhelming majority）。本文是①。
items.example: The amount of information online can be overwhelming for beginners.
items.trans: 網路上的資訊量對初學者來說可能多到令人難以招架。

items.usage: 放在名詞後面，強調「兩者皆然」，很道地的寫法。
items.example: The new policy has been criticized by teachers and parents alike.
items.trans: 新政策受到老師和家長一致的批評。

items.usage: 文章開頭吸引讀者的經典手法，注意 imagine 後接動名詞。可搭配 #99 Think how…。
items.example: Imagine working in an office with no internet connection.
items.trans: 想像一下在沒有網路的辦公室工作。

items.usage: 對應 as many/much as（多達）。文中強調「才不過 60 年前」。
items.example: You can start investing with as little as $100.
items.trans: 你只要 100 美元就能開始投資。

items.term: Add to that + N, and we see…
items.usage: 補充論點、層層推進的寫法，正式寫作和簡報都很好用。
items.example: Rents have doubled in five years. Add to that rising food prices, and it's no wonder young people are struggling.
items.trans: 房租五年內翻倍。再加上食物價格上漲，難怪年輕人過得很辛苦。

items.term: no one + N + can possibly + V
items.usage: no one 當形容詞修飾名詞，強調「單靠任何一個都不行」；possibly 加強否定語氣。
items.example: No one person can possibly handle all these responsibilities.
items.trans: 沒有任何一個人有辦法獨自扛下這些責任。

items.usage: 表示「達成某目標的前提」，主要子句常有 must / need / is needed。比 if we want to 正式。
items.example: We need to cut costs if we are to survive the downturn.
items.trans: 如果我們想撐過這波景氣低迷，就必須削減成本。

items.usage: 較正式，受詞常為 success / resistance / opposition / an accident / criticism。注意與「和某人見面」的 meet with someone 區分。
items.example: The proposal met with strong resistance from the board.
items.trans: 這項提案遭到董事會強烈反對。

items.usage: dire 意為「極其嚴重、危急的」，常見 dire consequences（嚴重後果）、in dire need of（急需）、dire warning（嚴正警告）。
items.example: The hospital is in dire need of more nurses.
items.trans: 這家醫院急需更多護理師。

items.usage: copious 偏正式，常搭 notes、amounts。take copious notes 是「做詳盡的筆記」。
items.example: She took copious notes during the training session.
items.trans: 她在培訓課程中做了詳盡的筆記。

items.usage: 文中 with scary regularity 帶點戲謔，常見替換 with alarming / surprising / monotonous regularity。
items.example: The train breaks down with alarming regularity.
items.trans: 這班列車故障的頻率高得驚人。

items.usage: 注意方向：「原因 + result in + 結果」；反過來是「結果 + result from + 原因」。與 #139 as a result of 互補。
items.example: A single typo in the code resulted in a system-wide outage.
items.trans: 程式碼裡的一個錯字導致整個系統停擺。

items.usage: 常見 It's not as easy as it sounds.（沒有聽起來那麼簡單），口語寫作都好用。
items.example: Running a café isn't as relaxing as it sounds.
items.trans: 經營咖啡店並不像聽起來那麼悠閒。

items.usage: = serve as，強調功能。
items.example: The spare bedroom also functions as a home office.
items.trans: 那間客房也兼作家庭辦公室。

items.usage: 比喻「防止失誤或損失的保障」，常見 provide a safety net、financial safety net。
items.example: An emergency fund acts as a safety net if you lose your job.
items.trans: 緊急預備金在你失業時能發揮安全網的作用。

items.usage: proceed 比 continue / go on 正式；proceed with + N（繼續進行某事）、proceed to + V（接著去做）。
items.example: Please read the terms carefully before you proceed any further.
items.trans: 在繼續之前，請仔細閱讀條款。

items.usage: check something off (the list)，完成一項就劃掉一項。英式英文常用 tick off。
items.example: I like to check off each task as soon as I finish it.
items.trans: 我喜歡每完成一項任務就馬上把它劃掉。

items.usage: 原意是「配備」，引申為「具備能力或條件」。也常見 be well-equipped to、be ill-equipped to（沒能力應付）。
items.example: Many schools are ill-equipped to support students with special needs.
items.trans: 許多學校沒有足夠的條件支援有特殊需求的學生。

items.usage: 注意介系詞用 to。
items.example: This species of bird is unique to Taiwan.
items.trans: 這種鳥是台灣特有種。

items.usage: nasty 意為「令人不快的、惡劣的」，相對於 a pleasant surprise。也可說 come as a nasty surprise。
items.example: The huge phone bill came as a nasty surprise.
items.trans: 那張巨額電話帳單讓人措手不及。

items.usage: 醫療常用字，動詞 make an incision。相關字 incisive（犀利的、一針見血的），可形容評論或分析。
items.example: The surgeon made a small incision just below the ribs.
items.trans: 外科醫生在肋骨下方開了一個小切口。

items.usage: 比 important 更強烈，常見 play a crucial role in、It is crucial that…。與 #57 vital 同級。
items.example: The first five minutes of an interview are crucial.
items.trans: 面試的前五分鐘至關重要。

items.usage: 受詞常為 a problem / an issue / a challenge，帶有「積極面對」的感覺，比 deal with 更主動。
items.example: The government has pledged to tackle youth unemployment.
items.trans: 政府承諾要解決青年失業問題。

items.usage: 常見 easily avoidable、entirely avoidable；反義字 unavoidable、inevitable。
items.example: The delay was entirely avoidable if we had planned ahead.
items.trans: 要是我們事先規劃好，這次延誤完全可以避免。

items.term: It was only after + N/子句 + that + 子句
items.usage: 強調句型，把重點放在「時間點」，比 We didn't notice until… 更有戲劇性。
items.example: It was only after I moved abroad that I realized how much I missed home cooking.
items.trans: 直到我搬到國外，才發現自己有多想念家常菜。

items.usage: 文中 it is the obvious steps… that are often most crucial，把「顯而易見的步驟」放到焦點位置。
items.example: It is not the price but the service that keeps customers coming back.
items.trans: 讓客人一再回流的不是價格，而是服務。

items.term: If + S + had p.p., S + would have p.p.
items.meaning: 如果當時……，就會……（與過去事實相反）
items.usage: 假設語氣第三類，用於檢討過去、分析「本可以如何」。變化版見 #82。
items.example: If we had backed up the files, we wouldn't have lost a week's work.
items.trans: 如果我們當時有備份檔案，就不會損失一整週的工作成果了。

items.usage: 帶有「瞧不起、不當一回事」的意味，常用 It's easy to scoff at…（很容易對……不屑一顧）。
items.example: Many people scoffed at the idea of online shopping in the 1990s.
items.trans: 1990 年代，很多人對網購這個點子嗤之以鼻。

items.usage: 帶貶意，指某物被包裝得很好聽，本質卻很普通。非常道地的口語寫法。
items.example: His job title is "logistics coordinator," but he's really just a glorified delivery driver.
items.trans: 他的職稱是「物流協調員」，但其實只是個名號好聽的送貨司機。

items.usage: killer 當形容詞，可指「極具殺傷力（重要）」或「超棒的」。常見 killer app、killer feature、killer question。
items.example: The camera is the killer feature of this new phone.
items.trans: 相機是這支新手機的殺手級功能。

items.usage: veteran 除了「退伍軍人」，放名詞前表示「經驗豐富的」，如 veteran journalist / actor / teacher。
items.example: The project is led by a veteran engineer with 30 years of experience.
items.trans: 這個專案由一位擁有 30 年經驗的資深工程師帶領。

items.usage: go through a list / the details / the contract。另一常見意思是「經歷（困難）」：go through a tough time。與 #107 run through 相近。
items.example: Let's go through the agenda before the meeting starts.
items.trans: 會議開始前，我們先把議程過一遍吧。

items.usage: read out + N 或 read + N + out。也可說 read aloud。
items.example: The teacher read out the names of the students who passed.
items.trans: 老師唸出了及格學生的名字。

items.usage: 文中 checking them off as they went 指「邊做邊打勾」。常見 learn as you go（邊做邊學）、make it up as you go（見機行事）。
items.example: Don't worry about memorizing everything—you'll pick it up as you go.
items.trans: 別擔心要記住所有東西，你會邊做邊學會的。

items.usage: 比 be careful to 正式，強調刻意留心。
items.example: Please take care to lock the door when you leave the office.
items.trans: 離開辦公室時請記得鎖門。

items.usage: 常見 leave no room for error / doubt / misunderstanding；正面說法 leave room for improvement（有改進空間）。
items.example: The contract was written to leave no room for misinterpretation.
items.trans: 這份合約的寫法不留任何誤解的空間。

items.usage: 放名詞前通常加連字號：a user-friendly interface；放 be 動詞後可不加。延伸用法 eco-friendly、budget-friendly。
items.example: The new booking system is much more user-friendly than the old one.
items.trans: 新的訂位系統比舊的好用多了。

items.usage: 文中 scrawled reminders 指「隨手潦草寫下的提醒」。近義字 scribble。
items.example: She scrawled her phone number on a napkin.
items.trans: 她把電話號碼潦草地寫在一張餐巾紙上。

items.usage: 常與 clear 連用：clear and concise。名詞 conciseness。
items.example: Keep your emails concise—most people only read the first few lines.
items.trans: 信件要寫得簡潔扼要，大部分人只會看前幾行。

items.usage: 比 ignore 正式，常見 disregard the rules / warnings；名詞 with complete disregard for（完全不顧……）。
items.example: He drove with complete disregard for the speed limit.
items.trans: 他開車完全無視速限。

items.usage: 可指真正的災害，也常用來誇張形容「結果很慘」：a disastrous first date。
items.example: The product launch was disastrous—the website crashed within minutes.
items.trans: 這次產品發表會慘不忍睹，網站幾分鐘內就當機了。

items.usage: 常見 a thorough investigation / check / review；副詞 thoroughly（thoroughly enjoyed 非常享受）。
items.example: The police carried out a thorough search of the building.
items.trans: 警方對大樓進行了徹底搜查。

items.meaning: 極其重要的、不可或缺的
items.usage: 與 #36 crucial 同級，常見 play a vital role、It is vital that…、vital signs（生命徵象）。
items.example: Regular maintenance is vital to keeping the machines running smoothly.
items.trans: 定期保養對機器順暢運作至關重要。

items.meaning: 實施、執行（計畫、政策、系統）
items.usage: 商務高頻字，受詞常為 a policy / a system / changes / a strategy；名詞 implementation。
items.example: The company plans to implement a four-day workweek next year.
items.trans: 公司計畫明年實施每週四天工作制。

items.term: It's easy to + V, particularly as…
items.usage: 先承認某種常見想法，再用 However 反駁，是議論文開頭的好用架構。與 #118 同類。
items.example: It's easy to dismiss small savings, particularly as prices keep rising. However, they add up over time.
items.trans: 小額儲蓄很容易被忽略，尤其是物價持續上漲的時候。但長期下來，這些錢會累積起來。

items.term: rather than V-ing – as + 主詞 + had intended – …
items.meaning: 而不是像某人原本打算的那樣……
items.usage: 用破折號插入 as X had intended，點出「實際做法」與「原本意圖」的落差。
items.example: The team rushed to finish the report rather than reviewing each section carefully, as the manager had intended.
items.trans: 團隊急著趕完報告，而沒有照經理原本的意思逐段仔細審閱。

items.term: The next time + 子句, + 祈使句
items.usage: The next time 直接當連接詞，不需要 when。適合文章結尾的行動呼籲。
items.example: The next time you feel stressed, try taking a short walk outside.
items.trans: 下次覺得有壓力時，試著到外面散散步。

items.usage: stride 是「邁大步走」，帶有自信、果斷的感覺。過去式 strode。另有片語 take something in stride（從容應對）。
items.example: She strode into the meeting room and took charge immediately.
items.trans: 她大步走進會議室，立刻掌控了局面。

items.usage: 源自莎士比亞《馬克白》，指「一次就（把所有事）解決」，可正面也可負面。
items.example: The new law eliminated dozens of outdated regulations in one fell swoop.
items.trans: 新法一舉廢除了數十條過時的規定。

items.usage: 文中 it is the team that really counts 的 count = matter。常見 Every vote counts.、What counts is…（重要的是……）。
items.example: It's not how much you earn that counts, but how you spend it.
items.trans: 重要的不是你賺多少，而是你怎麼花。

items.meaning: 從 A 到 B 無所不包
items.usage: 強調範圍廣，A 和 B 通常是差異很大的兩端。同家族見 #105、#140。
items.example: The store sells everything from groceries to garden furniture.
items.trans: 這家店從日常雜貨到庭園家具什麼都賣。

items.usage: 常用來謙虛地分享功勞：It was a team effort.
items.example: Winning the contract was a team effort—everyone played a part.
items.trans: 拿下這份合約是團隊共同努力的成果，每個人都有貢獻。

items.usage: 常見 thanks to the combined efforts of…（多虧了……的共同努力）。
items.example: The fire was put out thanks to the combined efforts of firefighters and local volunteers.
items.trans: 多虧了消防員和當地志工的共同努力，火勢才被撲滅。

items.meaning: （消息、結果）傳來；（承諾、表現）兌現
items.usage: 文中指資訊陸續傳來。也可指「做到」：She always comes through for her team.（她總能為團隊交出成果）。
items.example: We're still waiting for the test results to come through.
items.trans: 我們還在等檢驗結果出來。

items.usage: evident = clear / obvious，偏正式。也常見 It is evident from… that…。
items.example: It soon became evident that the project was over budget.
items.trans: 很快就看得出來這個專案超出預算了。

items.usage: 受詞多為困難：be faced with a choice / a crisis / pressure。主動用法 face + N 也行。
items.example: Small businesses are faced with rising costs and falling demand.
items.trans: 小型企業正面臨成本上升與需求下滑的困境。

items.usage: 用來對比兩者，比 instead of 更強調差異，寫作很好用。
items.example: I prefer to work in the morning, as opposed to late at night.
items.trans: 我偏好早上工作，而不是熬夜。

items.usage: 文中 can no longer be left to a lone hero 指「不能再全靠一位孤膽英雄」。常見 leave it to me、be left to chance（聽天由命）。
items.example: Important decisions shouldn't be left to chance.
items.trans: 重要的決定不該交給運氣。

items.usage: 可形容情況、對手、名聲：a fearsome reputation（令人畏懼的名聲）。
items.example: The team faces a fearsome opponent in the final.
items.trans: 這支隊伍在決賽中將面對一個可怕的對手。

items.usage: 比 attractive 更有「讓人忍不住被吸引」的感覺，常形容想法、提議、香氣。
items.example: The idea of working from a tropical beach is alluring, but the reality is less glamorous.
items.trans: 在熱帶海灘工作的想法很誘人，但現實沒那麼光鮮。

items.usage: 商務常用，受詞常為 a project / operations / a team。過去式 oversaw，過去分詞 overseen。名詞見 #150 oversight。
items.example: She was hired to oversee the company's expansion into Southeast Asia.
items.trans: 她受聘負責監督公司在東南亞的擴張。

items.usage: 原意是「敬禮」，引申為公開表揚：salute someone as…（稱頌某人為……）。
items.example: The mayor saluted the volunteers for their hard work.
items.trans: 市長向志工們的辛勞致敬。

items.usage: 常見 a miraculous recovery / escape；副詞 miraculously（Miraculously, no one was hurt.）。
items.example: Doctors described his recovery as nothing short of miraculous.
items.trans: 醫生形容他的康復簡直是奇蹟。

items.meaning: 經歷、接受（手術、變化、檢查）
items.usage: 受詞常為 surgery / treatment / changes / a test。過去式 underwent。
items.example: The company is undergoing major restructuring.
items.trans: 這家公司正在進行大規模重組。

items.usage: 可接名詞或 that 子句，偏正式。商務信件常用 acknowledge receipt of（確認收到）。
items.example: He acknowledged that he had underestimated the difficulty of the task.
items.trans: 他承認自己低估了這項任務的難度。

items.usage: 只能放名詞前：a lone survivor、a lone voice（唯一的反對聲音）。lone wolf 指「獨行俠」。
items.example: She was the lone voice of dissent at the meeting.
items.trans: 她是會議上唯一提出異議的人。

items.term: There was a time (in…) when + 子句
items.usage: 用來對比過去與現在，後面常接 These days, however,…。
items.example: There was a time when owning a mobile phone was a luxury. These days, however, almost everyone has one.
items.trans: 曾經有一段時期，擁有手機是種奢侈。然而如今幾乎人手一支。

items.term: S + would not have p.p. + as + adv. + as it did + without…
items.meaning: 要不是有……，就不可能（像實際上那樣）……
items.usage: 假設語氣第三類的變化版（見 #41），用 without 取代 if 子句，強調某因素的關鍵性。
items.example: The event would not have run as smoothly as it did without our volunteers.
items.trans: 要不是有志工們，活動不可能進行得這麼順利。

items.usage: 字面指接手駕駛，引申為「接管、掌控局面」。類似說法 take the wheel、take control (of)。
items.example: When the manager fell ill, his deputy took the controls and kept the project on track.
items.trans: 經理生病時，副手接手掌舵，讓專案維持在正軌上。

items.usage: 口語常用，後面可直接接 when / what / how to…。與 #4 be clueless about 同一家族。
items.example: I have no clue how to fix this printer.
items.trans: 我完全不知道怎麼修這台印表機。

items.usage: 可指「目的」（aimed at reducing costs），也可指「對象」（aimed at young professionals）。
items.example: The new policy is aimed at reducing employee turnover.
items.trans: 新政策的目的是降低員工流動率。

items.usage: 常搭配 improve / restrict / control the flow of information。
items.example: Weekly stand-up meetings help improve the flow of information across departments.
items.trans: 每週站立會議有助於改善跨部門的資訊流通。

items.meaning: 查看、確認（某人或某事的狀況）
items.usage: check on 強調「去看看狀況如何」：check on the kids、check on the progress。
items.example: I'll call the supplier to check on the status of our order.
items.trans: 我會打電話給供應商確認我們訂單的進度。

items.usage: advance = move forward，比 go to 正式。也常見 advance to the final（晉級決賽）。
items.example: Only three candidates will advance to the next stage of the interview process.
items.trans: 只有三位應徵者能進入下一階段的面試。

items.usage: 學術與報告常用，強調「統計上有關聯」，不一定是因果。名詞 correlation（a strong correlation between A and B）。
items.example: Higher levels of education tend to correlate with higher incomes.
items.trans: 較高的教育程度往往與較高的收入相關。

items.usage: 較常見的說法是 under pressure、in high-pressure situations；perform well under pressure 是履歷和面試常用語。
items.example: We need someone who can stay calm and make sound decisions under pressure.
items.trans: 我們需要一個能在壓力下保持冷靜、做出明智決定的人。

items.usage: 正式用字，受詞常為 a survey / an interview / research / an inspection / a safety check。注意名詞重音在前 /ˈkɑːn.dʌkt/。
items.example: The company conducts an employee satisfaction survey every year.
items.trans: 公司每年都會進行員工滿意度調查。

items.usage: 原指「無接縫的」，引申為「銜接完美、毫無阻礙」。常見 seamless transition / integration / experience。
items.example: Our goal is to ensure a seamless transition to the new system.
items.trans: 我們的目標是確保順利無縫地轉換到新系統。

items.usage: 比 improve 正式，常指「使原本好的更好」。受詞常為 performance / quality / reputation / experience。
items.example: The renovation greatly enhanced the hotel's appeal to younger travelers.
items.trans: 這次翻修大幅提升了飯店對年輕旅客的吸引力。

items.usage: 動詞 outline a plan / the main points；名詞 in outline（概略地）。
items.example: In her presentation, she outlined three key strategies for next year.
items.trans: 她在簡報中概述了明年的三項關鍵策略。

items.usage: collaborate with + 人 + on + 事。名詞 collaboration，形容詞 collaborative。
items.example: Our design team is collaborating with a Japanese firm on the new product.
items.trans: 我們的設計團隊正與一家日本公司合作開發新產品。

items.meaning: （團隊）簡短的碰頭會議；聚在一起
items.usage: 源自美式足球的「圍成一圈討論戰術」，職場上指快速的小組討論：have a quick huddle。
items.example: Let's have a quick huddle before the client arrives.
items.trans: 客戶到之前，我們先快速碰個頭吧。

items.usage: = compulsory / required，反義字 optional。常見 mandatory training / attendance。
items.example: Attendance at the safety training is mandatory for all new staff.
items.trans: 所有新進員工都必須參加安全培訓。

items.usage: 常見於流程、系統文件：predefined criteria / templates / rules。同類字 predetermined、preset。
items.example: Applications are screened against a set of predefined criteria.
items.trans: 申請案件會依照一套預先設定的標準進行篩選。

items.term: Think how + adj. + it would be if + 過去式…
items.usage: 假設語氣第二類，讓讀者想像情境、強化論點。與 #17 Imagine + V-ing 搭配效果更好。
items.example: Think how stressful it would be if you lost your phone on a business trip.
items.trans: 想想看，如果你出差時弄丟手機，那會有多焦慮。

items.usage: 用「讓步＋條件」強調前提的必要性。unless 子句用現在式表未來。
items.example: You can have the best product on the market, but unless people know about it, it won't sell.
items.trans: 你可以擁有市面上最好的產品，但除非大家知道它，否則賣不出去。

items.term: A do not + V + as well as those who do
items.meaning: A 不如那些有……的人做得好
items.usage: 用 those who do 省略重複的動詞片語，是精簡比較句的好寫法。
items.example: Employees who skip breaks often don't perform as well as those who do.
items.trans: 不休息的員工，表現往往不如有休息的人。

items.term: make a significant impact on + N
items.usage: impact 前可換 huge / lasting / positive / little；介系詞用 on。也可說 have an impact on。
items.example: Remote work has made a significant impact on commercial real estate.
items.trans: 遠距工作對商用不動產造成了重大影響。

items.usage: 強調「結果出乎原本預期」或「最終落得」。後接 V-ing、介系詞片語或形容詞：end up in hospital、end up broke。
items.example: We planned a quick coffee but ended up talking for three hours.
items.trans: 我們本來只打算喝杯咖啡，結果聊了三個小時。

items.usage: 常放句首作分詞構句：Drawing inspiration from…, she designed…。也可說 take inspiration from。
items.example: The architect drew inspiration from traditional Japanese temples.
items.trans: 這位建築師從日本傳統寺廟中汲取靈感。

items.meaning: 範圍從 A 到 B
items.usage: 與 #65 everything from A to B 類似，但更正式，常接在名詞後作補充。
items.example: The course attracts students ranging from high school graduates to retirees.
items.trans: 這門課吸引了從高中畢業生到退休人士各個年齡層的學生。

items.usage: witness / experience / see something firsthand；形容詞 firsthand experience / account。
items.example: Visiting the factory allowed us to see firsthand how the products are made.
items.trans: 參觀工廠讓我們親眼看到產品是如何製造的。

items.usage: 與 #46 go through 相近，但更強調「快速瀏覽或排練」。名詞 a run-through（彩排）。
items.example: Let's run through the presentation one more time before the client meeting.
items.trans: 客戶會議前，我們再把簡報快速演練一遍吧。

items.term: it turns out (that)… / turn out to be
items.usage: 表示「事後才發現」，是敘事中非常道地的轉折語。
items.example: The restaurant we picked at random turned out to be one of the best in town.
items.trans: 我們隨便挑的那家餐廳，結果竟是城裡數一數二的好店。

items.meaning: 預留、撥出（時間、金錢、物資）
items.usage: set aside time / money / a budget for…。另一意思是「擱置（分歧）」：set aside our differences。
items.example: I try to set aside 20% of my salary for savings every month.
items.trans: 我每個月都盡量把薪水的兩成存起來。

items.usage: keep to the schedule / the rules / the budget / the point。keep to the point 是「不離題」。
items.example: Please keep to the time limit so that everyone gets a chance to speak.
items.trans: 請遵守時間限制，讓每個人都有機會發言。

items.term: mean the difference between A and B
items.meaning: 決定 A 或 B 的關鍵
items.usage: 最經典的是 mean the difference between life and death（攸關生死），也可替換：between success and failure。
items.example: In sales, a quick response can mean the difference between winning and losing a client.
items.trans: 在業務工作上，回覆速度可能決定你是拿下還是失去一位客戶。

items.usage: ①官方或組織推動的計畫：a government initiative；②主動精神：take the initiative、show initiative。
items.example: Employees are encouraged to take the initiative and suggest improvements.
items.trans: 公司鼓勵員工主動提出改進建議。

items.usage: = deadly / fatal（#10）。常見 a lethal dose（致死劑量）；也可誇張形容 a lethal combination。
items.example: Some mushrooms contain toxins that are lethal even in small amounts.
items.trans: 有些蕈類含有即使少量也會致命的毒素。

items.usage: 除了「雇用」，正式寫作中 employ = use，受詞常為 a method / strategy / technique。
items.example: The researchers employed a new method to analyze the data.
items.trans: 研究人員採用了一種新方法來分析資料。

items.usage: 不能用被動或進行式（✗ is consisted of）。近義：be made up of、be composed of。
items.example: The committee consists of five members from different departments.
items.trans: 委員會由五位來自不同部門的成員組成。

items.usage: 程度比 surprising 強，常形容結果、數字、成就。近義 astonishing / staggering。
items.example: The app gained an astounding ten million users in its first month.
items.trans: 這款應用程式上線首月就獲得驚人的一千萬名用戶。

items.usage: 除了目擊事件，也可抽象地指「見證（變化）」：The city has witnessed rapid growth.
items.example: The past decade has witnessed a dramatic shift in how people consume news.
items.trans: 過去十年見證了人們獲取新聞方式的劇烈轉變。

items.term: It's hard to imagine that…, Yet…
items.usage: 先表達懷疑，再用 Yet 推翻，製造反差感。與 #59 是同一類開頭技巧。
items.example: It's hard to imagine that a ten-minute walk could improve your mood. Yet studies show it does.
items.trans: 很難想像散步十分鐘就能改善心情，然而研究顯示確實如此。

items.usage: in case 後接直述句（現在式表未來），表「預防」；注意與 if 不同：Take an umbrella in case it rains.（帶傘以防下雨）≠ if it rains（下雨的話才帶）。
items.example: I always save a backup copy in case my laptop crashes.
items.trans: 我總會存一份備份，以防筆電當機。

items.term: not only A but (may) also B
items.usage: 文中加入 may 讓第二部分語氣更委婉。注意兩邊結構要對稱。
items.example: Learning a second language is not only useful for your career but may also delay cognitive decline.
items.trans: 學第二語言不只對職涯有幫助，還可能延緩認知退化。

items.usage: 舉例的道地開頭，比 For example, 更生動。也可說 Take X, for example.
items.example: Take, for instance, Japan: its population has been shrinking for over a decade.
items.trans: 就拿日本來說吧，它的人口已經持續減少超過十年了。

items.usage: 先用大家熟悉的稱呼，再提出新觀點，常接 Yet… 轉折。
items.example: What most would call a hobby has become a full-time business for her.
items.trans: 大多數人眼中的嗜好，對她來說已經成了全職事業。

items.usage: be on display、put something on display；也可抽象指「表現出來」：Her talent was on full display.
items.example: The company's latest models are on display in the lobby.
items.trans: 公司最新的機型陳列在大廳。

items.usage: meet 的重要搭配：meet requirements / standards / expectations / deadlines / needs。商務高頻。
items.example: All products must meet strict safety standards before they can be sold.
items.trans: 所有產品都必須符合嚴格的安全標準才能販售。

items.usage: = It's no wonder that…，常用於歸納結論。也可說 come as no surprise。
items.example: Given how hard she works, it is no surprise that she got promoted so quickly.
items.trans: 看她那麼努力，難怪她升遷得這麼快。

items.usage: make 在這裡是「達到、進入」，如 make the team（入選隊伍）、make the cut（通過篩選）。
items.example: Only ten startups made the shortlist for the innovation award.
items.trans: 只有十家新創公司進入創新獎的決選名單。

items.term: give sb an edge over + N
items.usage: edge = 優勢，常見 a competitive edge（競爭優勢）、have the edge over。
items.example: Being fluent in Japanese gave her an edge over other applicants.
items.trans: 日語流利讓她比其他應徵者更有優勢。

items.usage: 口語，rake in 是「（像耙子一樣）大量收進」，big bucks 是「大錢」。也可單用 rake in profits / millions。
items.example: Top YouTubers can rake in the big bucks from sponsorship deals.
items.trans: 頂尖的 YouTuber 可以靠業配合作賺進大把鈔票。

items.usage: yield 原意「生產、產出」，常見 yield results / benefits / profits / a return。
items.example: The new marketing strategy has already begun to yield results.
items.trans: 新的行銷策略已經開始見效了。

items.usage: 主詞可以是事物：The job demands patience and attention to detail. 比 require 語氣更強。
items.example: Working in an emergency room demands quick thinking and a calm mind.
items.trans: 在急診室工作需要反應快、頭腦冷靜。

items.usage: enable + 人/物 + to + V，比 let / allow 正式，商務報告常用。
items.example: The new software enables us to process orders twice as fast.
items.trans: 新軟體讓我們處理訂單的速度快了一倍。

items.usage: 形容食物、設計、工藝、品味，帶有「細膩講究」的感覺。
items.example: The hotel is known for its exquisite service and attention to detail.
items.trans: 這家飯店以精緻的服務和對細節的重視聞名。

items.usage: 常見 a rash decision / promise、Don't do anything rash.（別衝動行事）。注意名詞 rash 是「疹子」。
items.example: Don't make any rash decisions while you're angry.
items.trans: 生氣的時候不要做任何衝動的決定。

items.usage: 常見 an uninformed decision / opinion；反義 informed（make an informed decision 做出明智的決定）。
items.example: Voters should avoid making uninformed choices based on rumors.
items.trans: 選民應避免根據謠言做出資訊不足的選擇。

items.usage: remain anonymous（保持匿名）、an anonymous donor / survey。名詞 anonymity。
items.example: The survey is completely anonymous, so please answer honestly.
items.trans: 這份問卷完全匿名，請誠實作答。

items.usage: 可形容人（不愛出風頭）或事物（外表樸素卻有實力）。
items.example: Behind its unassuming storefront is one of the city's best sushi bars.
items.trans: 在那不起眼的店面後面，藏著全城數一數二的壽司店。

items.usage: 形容工具、材料、人才都可以：a versatile actor、a versatile ingredient。
items.example: Eggs are one of the most versatile ingredients in the kitchen.
items.trans: 雞蛋是廚房裡用途最廣的食材之一。

items.usage: diverse settings / backgrounds / workforce；名詞 diversity。
items.example: Our team includes people from diverse cultural backgrounds.
items.trans: 我們團隊的成員來自多元的文化背景。

items.usage: 與 #26 result in 互補：「A result in B」=「B as a result of A」。正式寫作常用。
items.example: Several flights were cancelled as a result of the typhoon.
items.trans: 由於颱風，好幾個航班被取消了。

items.term: From A to B, + 主要子句
items.usage: 放句首總結範圍，常用於文章結尾強調「廣泛適用」。與 #65、#105 同屬「範圍」家族。
items.example: From managing schedules to tracking expenses, this app handles it all.
items.trans: 從管理行程到記帳，這款應用程式全都能搞定。

items.meaning: 精心設計的、製作精良的
items.usage: 可形容文章、計畫、產品：a well-crafted speech / strategy / email。同類複合字 well-designed、well-written。
items.example: A well-crafted cover letter can help you stand out from other applicants.
items.trans: 一封精心撰寫的求職信能幫你在眾多應徵者中脫穎而出。

items.usage: 非常高頻的道地用語，注意 to 是介系詞，後接名詞或動名詞。
items.example: When it comes to saving money, small habits make a big difference.
items.trans: 說到存錢，小習慣會帶來很大的差別。

items.usage: 主詞是「受益者」：Students will benefit from the new program. 反過來 A benefits B 是「A 讓 B 受益」。
items.example: Small businesses will benefit the most from the tax cuts.
items.trans: 小型企業將從這次減稅中獲益最多。

items.usage: 比單用 skip 更強調「略過不看或不處理」，常見 skip over the details。
items.example: Don't skip over the fine print when signing a contract.
items.trans: 簽合約時別略過小字條款。

items.meaning: 簡單、基本到看似蠢的事
items.usage: 口語，dumb = 笨的，stuff = 東西、事情。作者用來指「理所當然、容易被忽略的基本步驟」。注意 dumb 的 b 不發音。
items.example: Most accidents happen because people forget the dumb stuff, like checking the gas before leaving.
items.trans: 大多數意外都是因為人們忘了最基本的事，例如出門前檢查瓦斯。

items.usage: 放名詞後：the task / issue / problem at hand（眼前要處理的事）。也可指「近在手邊」：Keep your ID at hand.
items.example: Let's stop getting distracted and focus on the issue at hand.
items.trans: 我們別再分心了，專注在眼前的問題上吧。

items.usage: 字面是「從縫隙中溜走」，指事情或人在制度中被遺漏。也說 fall through the cracks。
items.example: With so many emails every day, important requests can easily slip through the cracks.
items.trans: 每天信件那麼多，重要的請求很容易被漏掉。

items.usage: 可指實際旅途，也常抽象指「在進行某事的過程中」：learn a lot along the way。
items.example: Starting a business is hard, and you'll make plenty of mistakes along the way.
items.trans: 創業很難，過程中你會犯不少錯。

items.usage: 強調「刻意騰出時間」；也常見 take the time to（願意花心思去做）。
items.example: Thank you for taking the time to meet with me today.
items.trans: 謝謝您今天撥冗與我見面。

items.usage: ①無心之過：It was an oversight on my part.（是我疏忽了）；②監督管理：regulatory oversight。與 #75 oversee 同源。
items.example: The missing data was due to a simple oversight, not intentional fraud.
items.trans: 資料缺漏是一時疏忽造成的，並非蓄意造假。

items.meaning: 可付諸行動的、具體可行的
items.usage: 商務高頻字，常見 actionable insights / advice / steps / feedback。
items.example: The consultant's report gave us clear, actionable recommendations.
items.trans: 顧問的報告給了我們明確且可執行的建議。

items.usage: 形容人：as stubborn as a mule（倔得像頭驢）；也可形容事物「難以去除的」：a stubborn stain、stubborn inflation。
items.example: He's too stubborn to admit he made a mistake.
items.trans: 他太固執了，不肯承認自己犯錯。

items.usage: 常見 falsely assume / claim / accuse。文中 falsely assuming that… 指「誤以為……」。
items.example: Many people falsely assume that working longer hours means being more productive.
items.trans: 很多人誤以為工作時間越長就代表越有生產力。

items.usage: = begin / start，但非常正式，常用於公告、法律、典禮。名詞 commencement（美國的畢業典禮）。
items.example: Construction is scheduled to commence next spring.
items.trans: 工程預定明年春天動工。

items.usage: 受詞常為 problems / difficulties / resistance，比 meet 或 face 正式。名詞 a chance encounter（偶遇）。
items.example: Please contact IT if you encounter any problems logging in.
items.trans: 如果登入時遇到任何問題，請聯絡資訊部門。

items.usage: #13 ineptitude 的形容詞。文中 the inept 是「the + 形容詞」表示一群人，如 the rich、the elderly。
items.example: The company collapsed under a series of inept managers.
items.trans: 在一連串無能經理人的領導下，這家公司垮了。

items.term: (Are you) Still + V-ing…, despite + N? + 祈使句!
items.usage: 省略主詞與助動詞的口語問句，常見於標題、廣告和文章小標，用來直擊讀者痛點。
items.example: Still struggling to wake up early, despite setting five alarms? Try going to bed an hour earlier!
items.trans: 設了五個鬧鐘還是爬不起來嗎？試試早一小時上床睡覺吧！

items.usage: 委婉地暗示好結果，just 讓語氣更輕鬆、帶點「說不定會有驚喜」的感覺。
items.example: Give the book a chance—you just might find you enjoy it.
items.trans: 給這本書一個機會吧，說不定你會發現自己挺喜歡的。

items.usage: 使役動詞，常用於指示他人做事，語氣比 make 溫和、比 ask 直接。
items.example: Have each participant write down one question before the session begins.
items.trans: 在課程開始前，請每位參加者寫下一個問題。
